correctness.rationale: Regenerative occupation measures π_off,π_on normalized by C=E(T+H) are finite because OU return mean hitting time grows only logarithmically at large |B_T| and is O(|B_T|) near zero. For p>0, Brownian occupation gives π_off(|x|^p) proportional to E[T^{1+p/2}]. The killed OU Poisson solution has derivative u_p′(y)=e^{ay²/(2D)}/D ∫_y∞ z^p e^{-az²/(2D)} dz; u_p(y)~y^p/(ap) for large y, so π_on moment finiteness is equivalent to E[T^{p/2}]. For Pareto survival, an exact Gaussian mixture gives the off tail amplitude (4D)^(δ−1)Γ(δ−1/2)/((δ−1)√π C). The absorbed OU forward flux identity Dq_on′+ax q_on=P(B_T>x)/C and endpoint Laplace asymptotics yield on amplitude (4D)^δ Γ(δ+1/2)/(2δ a√π C). Equality cutoff divergence follows from the exact Pareto moments. Optional stopping yields the already-known π_on(x²)=D/a. Independent numerical tests checked Gaussian mixture constants and the OU killed-flux relation; they do not prove regular variation.
